Normative requirement: Notify any actively exploited vulnerability contained in the product to the CSIRT designated as coordinator and to ENISA via the single reporting platform.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should define criteria and a decision workflow for identifying actively exploited vulnerabilities in TokenStream code, dependencies, containers, optional services, and integration paths; formal ENISA/CSIRT reporting is triggered only if the project enters CRA market-placement/manufacturer scope.
Preliminary applicability: Formal reporting conditional on legal scope; internal readiness applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: The current objective excludes CE marking and formal market placement, but TokenStream still needs a readiness path for actively exploited vulnerabilities because they drive urgent advisories, remediation, and user notification.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define what "contained in TokenStream" means for optional services, dependencies, deployment configs, and provider/MCP integrations.
Required security capability: Actively exploited vulnerability detection; reportability triage; ENISA/CSIRT reporting workflow trigger; evidence capture.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.1 Vulnerability Ingestion & Monitoring; §4.2 Risk Adjudication; §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §4.5 Art. 14 Notification RACI
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: reportability decision tree; vulnerability register; incident commander/RACI; single reporting platform runbook placeholder.

Normative requirement: Submit early warning for an actively exploited vulnerability without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, indicating affected Member States where applicable.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should have an internal 24-hour clock trigger for suspected actively exploited vulnerabilities, including awareness timestamp, affected versions, affected deployment channels, and geographic/user impact if known.
Preliminary applicability: Formal 24h reporting conditional on legal scope; internal clock readiness applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: Even if not formally reportable today, a 24-hour internal triage target helps preserve evidence and supports timely user notification for self-hosted operators.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define awareness criteria, severity triggers, and what information is realistically available within 24 hours.
Required security capability: Awareness timestamping; 24-hour early warning workflow; affected-version and affected-user assessment; evidence preservation.
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: intake timestamp; triage record; early warning template; affected deployment matrix.

Normative requirement: Submit vulnerability notification within 72 hours of awareness unless already provided, with product/exploit/vulnerability information, corrective or mitigating measures, user actions, and sensitivity indication.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain a 72-hour vulnerability notification package template covering TokenStream version/image/component identity, exploit nature, vulnerability description, mitigations, user actions, and sensitivity classification.
Preliminary applicability: Formal 72h reporting conditional on legal scope; internal readiness applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream users may need mitigation instructions quickly, and the project needs a structured way to move from initial awareness to actionable technical information.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define sensitivity handling and minimum information needed for operators without over-disclosing exploit details.
Required security capability: 72-hour report package; sensitivity classification; mitigation/user-action guidance; product identification.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.2 Risk Adjudication; §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §4.5 Art. 14 Notification RACI
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: 72-hour notification template; mitigation bulletin; sensitivity decision log; affected artifact list.

Normative requirement: Submit final vulnerability report no later than 14 days after a corrective or mitigating measure is available, including vulnerability description, severity/impact, malicious actor information where available, and details of security update or corrective measures.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should prepare a final vulnerability report/advisory package after a fix or mitigation, including severity, impact, affected versions, exploit evidence, fix details, user upgrade steps, and any known malicious activity.
Preliminary applicability: Formal 14-day final reporting conditional on legal scope; internal advisory readiness applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: This overlaps with public advisory needs and supports later evidence review even without formal reporting.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define severity/impact method and what actor/exploit information is safe and useful to disclose.
Required security capability: Final report; vulnerability severity and impact analysis; fix/mitigation documentation; advisory publication.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §6.1 Support Period & Update Obligations
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: final report template; GitHub Security Advisory; release notes; CVE/CVSS/EPSS notes if used.

Normative requirement: Notify any severe incident having an impact on the security of the product to the CSIRT designated as coordinator and ENISA via the single reporting platform.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should define severe security incident criteria for its self-hosted runtime, including compromise or suspected compromise of auth, admin APIs, API keys, corpora, provider/tool routes, ingestion pipeline, retrieval indexes, release artifacts, or update distribution.
Preliminary applicability: Formal incident reporting conditional on legal scope; internal incident readiness applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: The product can affect confidentiality, integrity, and availability of user-controlled corpora and connected tools. Severe incidents require a different workflow from ordinary bugs or vulnerabilities.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define severe incident scenarios and impact thresholds for TokenStream deployments.
Required security capability: Severe incident classification; incident response workflow; reportability triage; evidence preservation.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §4.5 Art. 14 Notification RACI; §8.1 CRA and NIS2
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: incident classification matrix; incident log; response runbook; reportability assessment.

Normative requirement: Submit early warning for a severe product-security incident without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, including whether unlawful or malicious acts are suspected and affected Member States where applicable.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should timestamp awareness of severe incidents and prepare an early internal incident report containing suspected malicious/unlawful cause, affected product versions, affected services, and known affected users or deployments.
Preliminary applicability: Formal 24h incident reporting conditional on legal scope; internal readiness applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: A disciplined early-warning step avoids losing incident facts and helps determine whether user notification is needed before full root-cause analysis is complete.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define awareness thresholds and what "severe" means for TokenStream.
Required security capability: 24-hour incident early warning; initial cause assessment; affected-user/deployment assessment; escalation.
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: incident intake form; awareness timestamp; initial severity assessment; escalation record.

Normative requirement: Submit incident notification within 72 hours of awareness unless already provided, including incident nature, initial assessment, corrective/mitigating measures taken, user measures, and sensitivity indication.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain a 72-hour incident notification template covering incident type, affected security properties, initial scope, mitigations, user actions, and sensitivity.
Preliminary applicability: Formal 72h incident reporting conditional on legal scope; internal readiness applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: Operators of TokenStream may need early mitigations such as rotating keys, disabling MCP tools, isolating services, upgrading images, or purging affected artifacts.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define incident sensitivity handling and minimum viable information for users.
Required security capability: 72-hour incident update; initial impact assessment; mitigation guidance; sensitivity handling.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §4.5 Art. 14 Notification RACI
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: 72-hour incident report template; mitigation instructions; user communication draft; sensitivity log.

Normative requirement: Submit final incident report within one month after the incident notification, including detailed description, severity/impact, likely threat or root cause, and applied/ongoing mitigations.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should produce a post-incident report for severe incidents, covering timeline, root cause, impact, severity, affected versions/deployments, mitigations, remaining risks, and follow-up actions.
Preliminary applicability: Formal one-month reporting conditional on legal scope; internal post-incident review applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: Post-incident review is needed to feed corrective actions, risk assessment updates, and control improvements.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define impact scoring and what incidents require risk reassessment.
Required security capability: Post-incident review; root-cause analysis; corrective action tracking; final report.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.3 Actionable Decisions; §4.4 Disclosure; §2.4 Sustainability & Review
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: post-incident report; timeline; RCA; corrective action tracker; risk assessment update.

Normative requirement: A product-security incident is severe if it negatively affects or is capable of negatively affecting availability, authenticity, integrity, or confidentiality of sensitive or important data or functions.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should classify incidents as severe when they affect or could affect API authentication, admin access, machine keys, provider credentials, corpora, source documents, retrieval indexes, policies, runtime snapshots, tool execution, or essential API availability.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable as internal severity criterion; formal reportability conditional on legal scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream's protected assets include sensitive user content and security-relevant configuration. This criterion directly maps to the product risk model.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define "sensitive or important data or functions" for TokenStream.
Required security capability: Severe incident criteria; asset criticality model; CIAA impact classification; reportability decision support.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.3 Actionable Decisions; §4.5 Art. 14 Notification RACI
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: critical asset list; severity matrix; incident classification examples.

Normative requirement: A product-security incident is severe if it led or could lead to introduction or execution of malicious code in the product or in users' network and information systems.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should treat parser exploitation, malicious ingestion artifacts, compromised container images, malicious MCP/tool execution paths, poisoned updates, or code execution in service containers/users' systems as severe incident candidates.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable as internal severity criterion; formal reportability conditional on legal scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream processes uploaded/remote content and can invoke tools/providers. Malicious code execution or introduction is a high-impact scenario for self-hosted deployments.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should identify code-execution and malicious-content threat scenarios.
Required security capability: Malicious-code incident classification; parser/tool sandboxing review; supply-chain incident detection; emergency mitigation.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.4 Secure Development Properties; §4.3 Actionable Decisions; §4.4 Disclosure
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: threat scenarios; parser security tests; image provenance records; incident decision log.

Normative requirement: Where necessary, the receiving CSIRT may request an intermediate report on relevant status updates about an actively exploited vulnerability or severe incident.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should be prepared to produce interim status updates for open vulnerability or incident response cases, including current status, mitigation progress, unresolved questions, and next update timing.
Preliminary applicability: Conditional on formal CSIRT request; internal readiness applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: Intermediate reports are essentially structured response updates. Maintaining them internally improves coordination even outside formal reporting.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define when unresolved high-risk cases require periodic updates.
Required security capability: Interim reporting; response status tracking; update cadence; stakeholder communication.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.5 Art. 14 Notification RACI; §4.3 Actionable Decisions
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: status update template; incident bridge notes; vulnerability case timeline.

Normative requirement: Submit Article 14(1) and 14(3) notifications via the single reporting platform using the electronic notification endpoint of the CSIRT designated as coordinator for the relevant Member State, simultaneously accessible to ENISA.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should document the future reporting-channel decision and avoid ad hoc email/manual reporting if formal CRA scope is triggered.
Preliminary applicability: Formal reporting channel conditional on legal scope; runbook placeholder applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: The single reporting platform is external to TokenStream, but the project needs a runbook to know where and how to submit if legal scope changes.
Risk assessment dependency: Legal role and establishment analysis determines the correct endpoint; risk assessment does not decide jurisdiction.
Required security capability: Reporting channel runbook; external platform access; submission responsibility; ENISA/CSIRT coordination.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §4.5 Art. 14 Notification RACI
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: reporting runbook placeholder; legal endpoint determination; responsible role list.

Normative requirement: Determine the relevant Member State endpoint based on main establishment in the Union; if none, use authorised representative, importer, distributor, or highest number of users hierarchy, with possible reuse of first CSIRT for subsequent reports.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain a legal-scope decision record for EU establishment/reporting endpoint only if the project moves into manufacturer/market-placement scope.
Preliminary applicability: Not applicable to current non-commercial OSS objective; legal-scope trigger only
Preliminary applicability rationale: The current scope has no CE marking and no formal market placement, so jurisdiction endpoint selection should remain a legal placeholder.
Risk assessment dependency: Legal scope and distribution model determine applicability; risk assessment may only inform user-location knowledge.
Required security capability: Regulatory endpoint determination; legal role analysis; user-location awareness where applicable.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.5 Product Assessment; §7.4 EU Authorized Representative
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates if future scope changes: EU establishment memo; AR/importer/distributor records; endpoint selection record.

Normative requirement: After becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability or severe product-security incident, inform impacted users, and where appropriate all users, of the vulnerability/incident and necessary risk mitigation or corrective measures, where appropriate in structured machine-readable format.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should notify affected users/operators through security advisories, release notes, documentation, mailing list or repository channels, and provide mitigation/upgrade actions; machine-readable advisory formats such as CSAF, CycloneDX VEX, or OpenVEX may be considered where useful.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary readiness scope; formal obligation conditional on legal scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: User notification is practical and important for OSS even if formal regulatory reporting is out of scope. Operators need to rotate secrets, upgrade, disable features, or apply mitigations quickly.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define affected-user identification, notification scope, and whether machine-readable formats are needed.
Required security capability: User notification; advisory publication; mitigation guidance; machine-readable vulnerability information; affected-version mapping.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.2 VEX; §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §7.2 Downstream Customer Provisioning
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: advisory template; VEX/CSAF/OpenVEX sample; release notes; mitigation guide.

Normative requirement: Commission delegated acts specify cybersecurity-related grounds for delaying dissemination of notifications under Article 16(2).
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should monitor delegated acts and define how to request or justify delayed dissemination if immediate dissemination could increase cybersecurity risk, especially during coordinated vulnerability disclosure.
Preliminary applicability: Conditional on formal reporting scope; standards/regulatory monitoring applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: Delayed dissemination is not controlled by TokenStream alone, but the project should be able to classify sensitivity and justify delay if future formal reporting applies.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should identify vulnerability classes where premature disclosure increases risk.
Required security capability: Regulatory monitoring; sensitive-information handling; delayed-dissemination justification; CVD coordination.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §4.5 Art. 14 Notification RACI
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: standards watch log; sensitivity classification; delayed-disclosure rationale template.

Normative requirement: Commission implementing acts may specify further format and procedures for Article 14, 15, and 16 notifications.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should monitor implementing acts and update reporting templates, data fields, and runbooks accordingly if formal scope is triggered.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable as regulatory monitoring readiness; formal reporting conditional on legal scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: Reporting formats may change as the single reporting platform matures. Templates should not freeze based only on current draft assumptions.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment does not set notification format, but it should provide data fields such as severity, impact, affected assets, and mitigations.
Required security capability: Regulatory monitoring; template maintenance; report data model; procedure update.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.7 Harmonized Standards Tracking; §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: reporting template version history; regulatory watch log; data field mapping.
